narrative.storyText: GRESB scoring builds cumulatively — every action stays in the score for future cycles, so this isn't a year-by-year sprint, it's a multi-cycle climb. Westbrook starts 2026 from a defendable position of 45 points (down from 2025's 52 because of retired indicators) and is targeting 62 — a confident 2-star outcome. Subsequent cycles push toward 3-star and eventually 4-star territory as specialist work and emerging scoring categories land. Below shows where each point comes from.
narrative.fivePillarCaveat: 5-star means top 20% of the ~2,200 global participants. With the global average sitting at 79 and rising ~3pts a year, the 5-star cutoff likely lands around 92+ by 2028. Reaching that requires sustained outperformance over many cycles — not something we'd chase prematurely. Strong, defensible 3-4 star outperformance builds more investor confidence than chasing a moving target.

sections.heading: What is GRESB?
paragraphs: GRESB (the Global Real Estate Sustainability Benchmark) is the industry-standard ESG scorecard for real estate. Around 2,200 funds submit globally each year.

Institutional investors — including NWPF — use it to compare ESG performance across their real estate holdings. For Westbrook, that makes a strong GRESB submission effectively a requirement, not a nice-to-have.

paragraphsAfterBulletsAfter: The cohort keeps improving — the global average rose ~3 points to 79 in 2025. A fixed score doesn't guarantee a fixed star outcome year-on-year.
